# The symptom

A tool call — e.g. `scheduler:get_next` — sends **no response and no progress for the
full 300s** MCP idle timeout, and the client aborts it:

> MCP server papercusp-su tool scheduler:get_next sent no response or progress for 300s; aborting

An **immediate retry of the identical call succeeds in ~2s**. No error ever surfaces from
the server itself. (Filed as EI-18167154191955470; the retry pattern is diagnostic.)

# The cause

An MCP tool handler that fans out to **unbounded** PG round-trips will block *silently* under
pool saturation. postgres.js **queues a query with no default timeout when every pooled
connection is busy** — so under contention the query sits waiting for a connection, producing
zero output, until something else frees a connection (or the client's 300s idle-abort fires
first). A heavy op — an `UPDATE ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` that must acquire *both* a
connection and a row lock — is the prime candidate.

This is a **failure-mode bug even when a retry recovers**: a silent 300s hang is
indistinguishable from a dead server, wastes 300s, and the abort is opaque. The underlying
*pool* contention is a separate concern (track/fix it on its own); this insight is about
making the tool **fail fast and legibly** regardless.

# The fix pattern

Wrap the heavy DB legs in [`withBoundedTimeout`](../../packages/operator-core/lib/bounded-timeout.ts)
(the same helper `fleet:status` uses for its fan-out reads) with a budget **well under the
300s client idle limit** (e.g. 30s ≈ 15× normal latency, 10× under the abort), and return a
**distinct, retryable** result on the deadline:

```ts
const claim = await withBoundedTimeout(getNextForBee({ /* … */ }), {
  fallback: null,              // type-correct; never read (branch on `degraded` first)
  timeoutMs: GET_NEXT_BUDGET_MS,
  label: 'scheduler:get_next:claim',
});
if (claim.degraded && claim.reason === 'error') throw new Error(claim.errorMessage);  // fail LOUD
if (claim.degraded) return timeoutResult();  // fail FAST: { ok:false, error:'timeout', retryable:true }
const res = claim.value;                     // normal path unchanged
```

Two guards that matter:

1. **Fail loud on a real error.** `withBoundedTimeout` swallows a *throw* into
   `{ degraded, reason:'error', errorMessage }`. Re-throw it — do **not** let a genuine DB
   error degrade into a false "no work / drained" miss. That silent conversion is its own bug.
2. **A timeout is not a drained lane.** Return a `error:'timeout', retryable:true` shape, and
   **never** set `windDown` / "drained" for it — a caller reading a false drain stands its
   loop down and reports a bogus all-clear.

# Caveat: it does not cancel the query

`withBoundedTimeout` is a `Promise.race`; it does **not** cancel the underlying query. So a
write (e.g. a claim `UPDATE`) that commits in the background *after* the deadline is a possible
orphan. That is acceptable when the orphan is **self-healing** — for `get_next`, the reconcile
+ lease-reclaim sweep at the top of the *very next* call frees it — **and** it already existed
under the old 300s hang; the bound only makes you fail faster. If a write has no such
self-healing path, prefer a DB-side `statement_timeout`/`lock_timeout` (transactional rollback,
no orphan) over a JS-level race.

# When to reach for this

Any MCP tool handler that makes one or more PG reads/writes with no internal budget — most of
them. Especially anything on a hot self-pull / fan-out path during a known pool-contention
regime. If a tool *can* hang to the 300s abort, it *will*, under load.
